Alex / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before the procurement team signs off we need a short write-up confirming the following for our Dedicated deployment:

- Can you confirm that our tenant will be logically and physically isolated to a single US region (no automatic cross-region replication)?
- If we request replication to a secondary region (for DR), can that be explicitly disabled per-tenant?
- Where do backups/snapshots reside by default and can they be configured to remain in-region only?
- For our data deletion policy: what is the timeline and evidence we get when we request a full tenant wipe (including snapshots, ephemeral caches, and any backups)?
- Is there an ability to exclude certain system snapshots from cross-tenant replication (we want to avoid our tenant artifacts being included in any replication bundles).

We're looking for clear operational steps and the types of artifacts you can provide (audit logs, signed attestation, playbook). If easier, we can do a short 30-minute call to go through each bullet.

Regards,

Ellen — great questions, thanks. I pulled together an initial summary below and attached a high-level infra diagram to illustrate the Dedicated tenant boundaries. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call; how does tomorrow 10am PT look?

Short answers (high level):
- Isolation: Dedicated deployments are deployed to customer-dedicated GPU pools in a single region by default; we do not enable cross-region replication unless explicitly requested and approved.
- Replication per-tenant: We support per-tenant replication controls. If you choose "in-region only" at provisioning, the control plane will mark snapshots/backups with a replication-exclude flag.
- Backups & snapshots: By default scheduled snapshots live in the same region. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature that is gated behind a DR request and contractual approval.
- Full tenant wipe: Our tenant-sanitization playbook covers ephemeral cache eviction, KV cache purge, deletion of model checkpoints and snapshots, and final metadata tombstone. Typical evidence we can provide: deletion audit logs, snapshot deletion receipts, and a runbook trace (engineer sign-off). Typical timeline: 0-24 hours for cache eviction, 24-72 hours for snapshot lifecycle termination depending on snapshot retention windows.
- Exclusion of system snapshots: We can apply tenant-scoped snapshot filters to avoid inclusion in aggregated replication bundles.

I'll loop in Karthik from infra so he can add the exact steps and the audit trail we can produce.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Hi Ellen — looping in the infra specifics below so you have a concrete playbook. I'll also upload the sanitized audit snippet and the formal wipe playbook to the shared drive after this message.

Technical summary (for FinServe Dedicated tenant):
1) Tenant isolation & replication controls
- Dedicated tenant is provisioned into a region-scoped cluster (US-West-2 in your case). No cross-region block-level replication is enabled by default.
- We expose a per-tenant flag "replication_scope": ["in-region", "disabled", "cross-region-DR"]. Provisioning with "disabled" or "in-region" prevents automatic cross-region snapshot copies.
2) Backups & snapshots
- Snapshot lifecycle: snapshots are created on scheduled windows and tagged with tenant_id and replication_scope. Snapshots are stored in our region-local object store (encrypted at rest).
- Snapshot retention windows are policy-driven; when a full tenant wipe is requested we trigger a snapshot-deletion job that marks snapshots for immediate garbage collection. If a snapshot is already queued for replication, the job first invalidates the replication manifest.
3) Ephemeral caches and runtime state
- KV caches and ephemeral model caches are tenant-scoped and cleared synchronously on wipe request; cache eviction is typically < 1 hour for active nodes and immediate for queued requests.
4) Deletion evidence and attestation
- We provide: deletion audit logs (timestamped event stream showing snapshot deletions, cache evictions, and checkpoint tombstones), S3 object deletion receipts, and an ops sign-off record.
- If required contractually, we can provide a signed attestation (PDF) stating the wipe was executed per the agreed playbook; this is typically delivered within 5 business days.
5) Edge cases and replication exclusion
- For aggregated replication bundles we have a filtering step during manifest generation that excludes snapshot entries tagged with replication_scope != "cross-region-DR". That prevents tenant artifacts from being batched into cross-region replicas.
6) Customer-managed KMS
- We support customer KMS keys so that even if an object were accidentally replicated, it would remain unreadable without your key; however we do not rely on that as the primary isolation control.

Artifacts we'll provide: sanitized audit log excerpt (CSV), wipe-playbook-v1.docx (detailed steps), and a timeline estimate for full irrevocable deletion. Link: https://drive.google.com/finserve/redwood/wipe-playbook

If that covers everything, I'll prepare the signed attestation template and the sample audit logs for procurement. Please confirm acceptance of the timeline and whether you need inclusion of the attest in the SOW.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
